ex: I have a seminar on marketing tomorrow.
What time does the seminar start today?
Can I sign up for the free seminar?
Our teacher gives a seminar every Friday morning.
You can change this parameter in the settings.
What parameters should I use for the test?
This function in the code takes two parameters.
We need to set clear parameters for the project.
My gaming setup cost a lot of money.
He showed us his new desk setup at home.
What do you think of my home office setup?
I need a better camera setup for my videos.
setup.note: The noun is one word; the verb is two words: "Set up the camera."

ex: The zoo tries to copy each animal's natural habitat.
Forests are an important habitat for many birds.
Pollution is destroying the habitat of these fish.
Where is the natural habitat of the polar bear?

phantom.note: "Ghost" is the more common everyday word.

ex: The cardinal wore a long red robe.
The cardinals meet in Rome to choose the pope.
A cardinal visited our city's cathedral last week.
Who is the youngest cardinal in the Catholic Church?
cardinal.note: Also a red North American bird, and an adjective meaning "most important": a cardinal rule.

comeback.note: Usually "make a comeback": The team made a great comeback.

ex: Does this truck run on diesel or gas?
Diesel is cheaper than gas here.
He bought a car with a diesel engine.
The price of diesel went up again.
diesel.note: Uncountable as fuel: "some diesel". A car with a diesel engine is "a diesel".

avant-garde.note: As a noun, usually "the avant-garde." Also an adjective: avant-garde art.

ex: The movie has a funny gag about a dog.
That old gag still makes me laugh every time.
Is this a real sign or just a gag?
The comedian ended his show with a great gag.
gag.note: Also a cloth over someone's mouth, and the verb "gag" means to almost throw up.

ex: A tornado hit the town last night.
The tornado destroyed many houses on our street.
We hid in the basement during the tornado.
Tornadoes are common in this state.
The circle has a radius of five centimeters.
Are there any stores within a one-mile radius?
Measure the radius to find the area.
This restaurant delivers food within a small radius.
This car is an import from Japan.
Most of our coffee is an import from Brazil.
Cheap imports are hurting local farmers this year.
Are these shoes local or an import?
import.note: Also a verb: "We import oil." Stress: IMport (noun), imPORT (verb).

script.note: Most often "script" means the text of a movie or play: "She wrote the script."

ex: We had chocolate pudding for dessert.
My kids love vanilla pudding after dinner.
She made rice pudding with cinnamon.
I bought pudding cups for lunch.
pudding.note: In the US, a soft sweet dessert like thick cream. In the UK, "pudding" can mean any dessert.

ex: We chose a new software vendor this year.
The company pays all its vendors on time.
Which vendor sells the best laptops for schools?
Ask the vendor about the price for support.
vendor.note: Also a person who sells things on the street: "a street vendor".

ex: Let's make popcorn and watch a movie.
I bought a large bag of popcorn at the theater.
The smell of popcorn filled the kitchen.
Do you want butter on your popcorn?
popcorn.note: Uncountable: some popcorn, a bag of popcorn (not "a popcorn").

ex: This game studio released five new titles this year.
The library added two hundred new titles last month.
What is the best-selling title in your store?
This anime title is very popular with teenagers.
title.note: Most often "title" means the name of a book or film: "What is the title of this song?"

ex: Bam! The door closed hard behind me.
I turned the key and, bam, the engine started.
Bam, the ball hit the window.
He opened the box and bam, a surprise.
bam.note: Informal. Used to say something happened suddenly and fast.

quarterback.note: A player in American football who throws the ball.

ex: Bravo! That was a beautiful song.
The audience shouted "Bravo!" at the end.
Bravo, you did a great job.
People in the front row stood up and shouted "Bravo!"
bravo.note: Used mostly at concerts and shows; "Well done!" is more common in daily life.

ex: She showed her design portfolio at the job interview.
Every artist needs a strong portfolio of work.
Can I see your portfolio before we start?
Add your best photos to your online portfolio.
portfolio.note: Very often "portfolio" means all the stocks and other investments a person has.

ex: Tourism is important for the local economy.
The city earns a lot from tourism.
Tourism grew after the new airport opened.
She studies tourism at a college in Kyiv.
tourism.note: Uncountable: tourism (not "a tourism"). A person is "a tourist."

ex: Follow the safety guidelines at work.
The company has strict guidelines for emails.
The new guidelines start next month.
Where can I find the guidelines for new workers?
guideline.note: Usually used in the plural: guidelines.

ex: Her brother is a soldier at the front.
He spent two years at the front.
We get news from the front every day.
A cold front will bring rain tomorrow.
front.note: Most often "front" means the front part: "Sit in the front." "in front of the house"

ex: Why did the referee call a foul there?
He got a yellow card for a foul.
That was a hard foul on the striker.
She has four fouls in the game.
foul.note: As an adjective, "foul" means very bad or dirty: "a foul smell."

ex: Send the file in PDF format.
What format is this video file in?
I don't like the new format of the show.
Please use this format for your report.
I made chicken curry for dinner.
This curry is too spicy for me.
Can we order some curry and rice tonight?
She learned to cook curry in India.
Do you like country music or rock?
She loves listening to country music in the car.
They play country music in this bar on Fridays.
My dad sings old country songs at parties.
country.note: Most often "country" means a state: "Ukraine is a big country."

guru.note: Often informal for an expert: "a tech guru".

ex: She got a dental implant last month.
How much does a dental implant cost here?
This small implant in his ear helps him hear.
The doctor removed the old implant from her knee.
My sister has worked in retail for five years.
Retail sales went up this month.
The retail price is twenty dollars.
Retail jobs are busy at Christmas.
retail.note: Often used before nouns: "retail price", "retail store".

ex: Many families depend on welfare to survive.
He was on welfare for two years.
The government wants to cut welfare programs again.
Welfare helps people who can't find work.
welfare.note: Also means health and safety: "animal welfare", "child welfare".

ex: The ship is in dock for repairs this month.
My father worked at the docks for twenty years.
Workers unload boxes from ships at the docks.
Big ships are built and repaired in this dock.
dock.note: In the US, "dock" often means a small wooden pier for boats: "Meet me at the dock."

depot.note: Often a place to store goods: "an oil depot". In the US, also a small bus or train station.

ex: Coffee is the main export of Brazil.
Our exports grew a lot last year.
The country depends on oil exports.
Is wine an important export in your country?
export.note: Also a verb: "We export grain." Stress: EXport (noun), exPORT (verb).

bartender.note: "Bartender" is the usual US word; "barman" is British.

ex: He is young and has very high ideals.
She always tries to live by her ideals.
Freedom is an important ideal for many people.
Is a big house your ideal of happiness?
ideal.note: Most often "ideal" is an adjective: "This is an ideal place for a picnic."
